TrustUI Screens · Living Master File · Design-System Aligned

From components to real screens — one file, continuously extended.

Every screen below is composed entirely from tokens and components already established in the Design System reference. Nothing new is invented at the token level here — this is composition, not a new aesthetic pass. This file now holds every iteration in sequence — Customer and Seller core flows, Desktop/Tablet adaptations, Entry, Trade Code discovery, buyer-initiated Trade creation, dispute Resolution, Seller/Business discovery profile, Trust History, Account, Categories, Support, seller-side Trust/Verification/Alerts, the TrustOps Proposal Review console, and the Park Agent TrustOps onboarding/lifecycle — rather than being split across separate versioned files.

Scope of this pass: mobile web only — customer (buyer) and seller flows, shown in a browser-chrome frame, not a native app bezel, consistent with the "mobile web first" decision. Desktop and tablet adaptations follow in the reference section; this pass extends Park Hub into a complete TrustOps-managed agent lifecycle and closes the operational gaps around custody, exceptions, access, and re-verification.

Terms of Service & Privacy Acceptance — Mobile Web · Complete Flow

Referenced by every signup since Entry was built, never actually shown

Two screens: consent during account creation, and the separate re-consent a returning user sees if terms change later — these can't be the same screen, since one is blocking a brand-new account and the other is interrupting someone with an active Trust Profile.

↑ Master index
TOS1
Review Terms & PrivacyDuring Sign Up — before the account is created
app.komtru.com/signup/terms
Terms & Privacy
1. What Komtru does

Komtru holds payment for a Trade between a buyer and seller until both sides fulfil what was agreed, and releases funds accordingly.

2. Fees

A Buyer Protection Fee (1.5% of item price) applies to every funded Trade. Logistics fees are shown separately before you pay.

3. Your data

We collect identity, transaction, and device information to verify participants and prevent fraud. We never sell your data to third parties.

4. Trust Profile

Your completed Trades, verification status, and dispute history form a Trust Profile visible to people you trade with — this can't be deleted while your account remains active.

5. Dispute resolution

Komtru TrustOps mediates disputes per published policy. Decisions can be appealed once per case.

Confirming releases payment for the iPhone now. The MacBook can go to dispute on its own — the rest of the order isn't held up by one item.

PART 3 Create & Propose a Trade
Create, configure, verify and negotiate a Traderef
Create a Trade · Model

A Trade is assembled, not filled in

Both parties contribute, each supplying only what they own, and Komtru applies category policy. Four stages — About, Item & delivery, Trade terms, Review — run for both entry points; the fields that appear depend on the role, the category and the delivery mode.

CategoryKomtru1Detected from the item or listing. Never asked.
Item specificationSeller2Category-driven (Electronics or Fashion & Luxury). The buyer sees it but cannot edit it; the accepted specification is the evidence in a dispute.
Delivery mode and destinationBuyer2Courier or Park. Park shows a Park chooser; Courier shows address and landmark. Only the chosen mode’s fields appear.

StageBuyer startsSeller starts
1 · About the tradeSeller, what you’re buying, agreed price. Category detected.Buyer by phone number, then a listing. Category and price from the listing.

4 · Review & sendProposal with the seller’s part outstanding.Proposal with the buyer’s choice outstanding.
Ownership rules: the seller is the only author of the item specification. The seller owns delivery cost and the delivery promise. Komtru owns inspection, cancellation, refund and return. The buyer owns the destination or Park.
Why a Trade is never finished by one person: a buyer cannot know the IMEI or the delivery cost, so Komtru asks the seller for them and shows exactly what is outstanding, instead of making the buyer invent them.

Trade Standards by Category — Mobile Web

Set by Komtru, the same for every seller in a category

Every screen up to this point let the seller or buyer pick an inspection window during Create Trade. That's now fixed by category instead — the same protection applies whether it's TechEdge NG or a brand-new electronics seller, and neither side can quietly negotiate it down. Buyers can still ask for longer, never shorter.

Fashion's shorter window reflects how fast wear, fit, and finish are actually easier to judge than a working electronic component — not a lower standard of protection.

Entry points and open policy values

Buyer Alerts (J4) open the return decision (RX-01) and the seller's counter-offer (RX-14); seller Alerts (M3) open the incoming return (RX-05) and the settlement offer (RX-13). Case status (CWT-S15) opens settlement (RX-12) and the Hub Dashboard opens return intake (RX-16). A replacement (RX-10, RX-11) is the alternative to a return for the same case, so it arrives through its own decision notification. RX-09 is time-triggered: it replaces RX-02 and RX-03 when the return window lapses. The return window length, who bears return shipping and fee treatment are design values; the authoritative figures come from category policy at execution.

Fast responder

The seller usually replies within an hour.

PART 8 Park Agent / Hub Mode
Park Agent, Hub registration, custody and Park operations9 mobile
Park Agent / Hub Mode — Mobile Web · New Persona

The third lens Komtru TrustOS needs — not just Buyer and Seller

Interstate trade in Nigeria moves through motor parks, not just courier riders. This turns a park clerk into a verified custody agent: log a parcel in, physically inspect it, and only release it when the buyer's Handover PIN matches — closing the exact gap that makes Park-and-bus delivery the easiest vector for scam "delivery."

Park Hub Registration & Onboarding — Mobile Web · Complete Flow

The "+ Register a Park Hub" button, followed through to a live hub

Mirrors the shape already established for Merchant onboarding — verify identity, prove legitimacy with mandatory evidence, set up payout, review, submit — adapted for a park clerk instead of a seller. Nothing here invents a new pattern: proof upload reuses the same mandatory-media gate as Seller Trade Acceptance, payout setup reuses Add Bank Account, and the review step reuses the Design System's evidence-and-decision case layout.

PART 11 TrustOps Console — Remaining Screens
PART 12 Desktop & Tablet Reference Adaptations
Desktop experienceprinciples
Desktop · Principles

Desktop is its own experience, not a wider phone

These screens are designed for a large, pointer-driven workspace. They share the Komtru design system and the pioneer desktop shell, but not the mobile layouts. Screens are grouped in the order a trade happens.

↑ Master index
Persistent context. A sidebar with the five tabs and a top bar with global search, Trade Code entry, the Buy / Sell switch, notifications and the account are always present.
Master-detail, not page-to-page. Lists stay visible while the detail changes; a context rail carries the next action, the money and the evidence.
Compare, don’t remember. Listing against offer, three agreement versions, seller proof against what arrived, and both sides’ evidence are shown side by side.
Volume work gets tables. Merchants sort, filter, select several and act once; bulk actions replace one-at-a-time cards.
Secondary tasks slide over. Reporting an issue opens beside the trade it is about, so context is never lost.
Chronological order. Sections 01 to 10 follow a trade from arrival to account. Buyer and merchant views appear at the stage where each acts.

Tablet experienceprinciples
Tablet · Principles

Tablet is a third interaction model

Tablets are touch-first like phones but have room for two panes like desktops. These screens use top navigation, list-and-detail pairs, modal sheets and sticky action bars. Screens are grouped in the order a trade happens.

↑ Master index
Touch first. Targets are 46px or larger; nothing depends on hover; primary actions sit in sticky bottom bars within thumb reach.
Top navigation, two panes. Five tabs across the top; lists open a detail pane beside them instead of a new screen, but the list is narrower than on desktop.
Modal sheets for secondary tasks. Reporting an issue is a sheet over the dimmed trade, sized for thumbs, rather than a slide-over.
Segmented, not side-by-side. Where desktop compares two things in two panes, tablet uses a segmented control to swap between them.
Chronological order. Sections 01 to 10 follow the same trade journey as the desktop group.

TrustOps consoleprinciples
TrustOps · Principles

An operations console that mirrors how Komtru works

Built for adoption: the console is organised around the same things the product creates, every area looks and behaves the same way, and nothing is decided without a person and a reason. Screens run in the order a reviewer’s day does, from starting the shift to searching the record.

↑ Master index
Organised the way Komtru works. People, Proposals, Trades, Money, Custody and Cases are the same objects the product creates, so a reviewer already knows the names.
Every row answers four questions. What happened, why it’s here, how long it has, and what to do next.
Every case has the same four zones. Evidence, what Komtru suggests, your decision with a reason, and the trail. Learn it once; it works for people, proposals, payments, parcels, disputes and appeals.
A person decides. Suggestions are labelled “not a decision”. Higher-risk actions need a second approver. Every decision is saved with who, why and when.
Always know where you are. The left pane collapses to icons, and every screen that isn’t a main destination has a back arrow naming where it returns to.
Desktop first, tablet for moving about. The tablet screens use the same areas and the same four zones, with larger controls and the decision in a sticky bar.
TrustOps console1 diagram
Operating model · The work engine

How work moves through TrustOps

One shape of work underlies every pillar. Automated, assisted and expert decisions share the same intake, the same clock and the same record.

↑ Master index
F0
The work engine
Every pillar handles the same shape of work: a signal arrives, is classified, goes to an automated, assisted or expert path, is decided with a reason, carried out, explained to the people involved, and learned from. The flows after this one are variations.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Rule
Waiting on a person pauses the clock and tells them; waiting on us never does.
Rule
No one approves their own work. Money and access changes need a second person.
Rule
Every step writes to the Trust Trail: who, what, why, when.
TrustOps console12 diagrams
Operating model · Flows by pillar

Who does what, and where it changes hands

Twelve flows, each a variation of the engine, showing the owner, the clock and the rule that must never be broken.

↑ Master index
F1
Identity & verification
Deciding who is who, once, so nobody is asked twice. Most people pass automatically; the rest are looked at by a person.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Verification officer
Clock
First response 4h · decision 24h
Never
Verification makes someone verified, not trusted.
F2
Trade proposal review
The first decision on a Trade: is it safe to let this proposal reach the other side?
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Case officer
Clock
First response 30 min · decision 4h
Target
Most proposals never reach a person.
F3
Money exceptions & settlement
Payments and payouts are matched automatically. Anything that doesn’t match is fixed by a finance officer, and every payout is prepared by one person and approved by another.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Finance officer
Clock
Exceptions: decision 2h
Never
Don’t pay again while a payment is unconfirmed.
F4
Custody exceptions
When a parcel at a hub is wrong: unsealed, missing, overdue, or the wrong one. The parcel is frozen first and questions come after.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Custody officer
Clock
Decision 4h; returns held over 24h are flagged
Never
Nothing is released from a frozen parcel without a reason.
F5
Disputes, returns & appeals
From “something’s wrong” to a fair outcome that is carried out, with a chance to settle first and a second look afterwards.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Case officer; senior over ₦500K
Clock
Decision 48h; return window 2d 20h
Never
Nothing pays out on its own if a window lapses; it returns to a person.
F6
Fraud & risk
Patterns, not accusations: related signals are grouped, a person reviews the history, and any restriction is small, reasoned, time-limited and explained.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Risk analyst
Clock
Review 4h · restrictions expire and are re-reviewed
Never
A restriction with no end date.
F7
Customer success & account recovery
The person contacts us. They are recognised, helped from a playbook, and routed to a specialist only when needed. Recovering an account takes extra care.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Support agent
Clock
First reply 15 min in hours · next morning after
Recovery
Lost phone or a suspected SIM swap: ID + a trusted device, never the SMS code alone.
F8
Compliance & legal
Screening hits, unusual patterns, data requests and legal requests are handled in restricted cases that only named people can open.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Compliance officer
Clock
Set by the obligation; tracked per case
Never
Compliance cases are not visible in general search.
F9
Shift handover & escalation
Work doesn’t stop overnight, so clocks and promises are handed over in writing, and a slipping clock climbs a fixed ladder.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Team lead
Rule
No item changes shift without an owner.
Emergency
Break-glass access needs a reason and is reviewed next day.
F10
Incident command
When something big goes wrong (a provider fails, a pattern spikes, a hub is compromised) one person is in charge and people are told plainly.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Incident commander
Rule
Never retry a payment until the provider confirms the first one failed.
Review
Every incident ends in a written review.
F11
Learning & change control
How what we learn becomes a rule: a finding becomes a tested, reviewed, signed-off change with a version and a date.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Quality & policy lead
Rule
Policies and thresholds change only through this flow.
Why
So a decision can always cite the version it used.
F12
Team access: join, move, leave
People get exactly the access their role needs, a second person approves the sensitive ones, and leavers lose access within the hour.
▢ where it starts▢ a person does this┄ the system does this▢ a decision point▢ where it ends
Owner
Admin
Rule
Admins manage access; they can’t decide cases or move money.
Audit
Every change is in the audit log.

Operating model · Decision rights & escalation

What is automatic, what needs a person, what climbs

Thresholds and the escalation ladder that apply across every area. All numbers are proposals to confirm.

↑ Master index
Decision rights: automated, assisted, expert
The Operating Model’s three tiers, made specific. Thresholds are proposals to confirm with operations, risk and finance.
DecisionAutomatedAssisted (a person, with a suggestion)Expert (specialist or two people)
Identity (individual)Provider matches BVN or NINMismatch or poor imageRepeated mismatches or linked identities
Business verificationNever fully automaticRegistration and documents matchName mismatch, or a high-value seller
Trade proposalLow risk, up to ₦200KFlagged, or ₦200K to ₦1MOver ₦1M, or high-risk signals
Payment confirmationReference and amount matchMismatchAdjustment or over ₦1M: two approvers
Payout releaseConfirmed delivery, no holdsHeld itemsOver ₦1M: two approvers
Custody exceptionOverdue reminderUnsealed or mismatchedTampering, or a repeat at one hub: incident
DisputeBoth sides agree a settlementUnder ₦500KOver ₦500K, or any appeal
Risk restrictionWatch (log only)Limit new ordersPause live Trades: analyst and lead
Account recoveryNever fully automaticID and a trusted device both matchSuspected SIM swap: risk and verification lead
Escalation ladder
A clock that’s slipping climbs the same ladder in every area. Waiting on a person pauses it; waiting on us doesn’t.
Clock usedWho is toldHowWhat happens
50%The ownerIn the appA nudge
80%The owner and the leadIn the app and pushThe lead sees it as at risk
100%The leadPush and SMSReassign or help; the person is told it’s taking longer
150%The ops headA callFind the cause; consider an incident
IncidentThe incident commanderEvery channelFlow F10

Park Agent, Hub registration, custody and Park operationsReference / architecture
Next beyond registration — Park Agent operating model

Turn Park Agents into a measurable custody network

Registration is the beginning. TrustOps should understand where parcels are, which hubs are under strain, which agents need attention and how custody performance changes over time.

↑ Master index

Network capacity

Rank hubs by held parcels and intake velocity; flag overloaded terminals before they become incidents.

Held parcel ageing

Use <6h, 6–24h, 24–48h and >48h buckets with escalation for ageing custody.

Agent performance

Track intake, PIN releases, failed attempts, inspection completion, incidents and custody duration.

Hub availability

Model open, closed, full, unable-to-receive and suspended states.

Audit & evidence

Every intake, inspection, release, freeze, reassignment and suspension becomes an immutable Trust Trail event.

Operational alerts

Surface ageing parcels, expiring authorization, agent changes and reopened incidents as actionable alerts.

Period comparisons

Week, month, quarter, year and custom range should drive period KPIs and charts, while lifetime remains explicitly all-time.

Access governance

Receive, inspect, release, staff management and payout administration remain separate permissions.

PART 13 Park Agent TrustOps Lifecycle & Gap Closure
Park Agent, Hub registration, custody and Park operations4 mobile
Park Agent / Hub — TrustOps-owned onboarding, activation & lifecycle

Park Hub registration is now a TrustOps case from first claim to every later re-verification

The existing PH1–PH6 flow correctly submits an application to TrustOps, but the product still reads like the applicant owns the lifecycle. This extension makes TrustOps the system of record: every Park Agent gets an application ID, an assigned reviewer, explicit evidence states, a controlled activation step, a role/permission record, and a re-verification path.

↑ Master index

Recommended lifecycle

Do not treat “approved” as the end of onboarding. A Park Hub is a custody role, so its trust state must remain inspectable and revocable.

1 · ClaimAgent starts or accepts an invitation for a specific hub.
2 · VerifyIdentity + phone + device anchor.
3 · Prove authorityPark affiliation, branch and authorization evidence.
4 · ConfigurePayout + operating hours + staff access.
5 · TrustOps reviewAI assists; a human approves, requests changes or rejects.
6 · ActivateHub and agent permissions unlock atomically.
7 · MonitorCustody events, exceptions and payout behaviour stay auditable.
8 · Re-verifyRole, authorization or risk changes can pause custody.

Park Agent, Hub registration, custody and Park operationsReference / architecture
Gap audit — recommended next screens

What I would add next, beyond the registration flow

These are the missing product states I found by following the Park Agent lifecycle end-to-end, not by changing the existing visual language.

↑ Master index

1. Agent invitation / claim

A hub should be an entity, while a person is an authorized operator. Support “You’ve been invited to operate Jibowu Hub” and prevent two people from silently creating duplicate hubs for the same terminal.

2. Changes requested loop

PH6 currently jumps from submitted to a binary TrustOps decision. Add a first-class “Changes requested” state so reviewers can ask for one precise document without forcing a full restart.

3. Hub vs. agent separation

Store Hub ID, Park/Operator, Branch, Primary Agent and Staff separately. This makes staff replacement possible without corrupting the custody history.

4. Permission model

Receive, inspect, release, add staff and manage payouts should not all be the same permission. Release rights should remain tied to verified identity and the PIN guard.

5. Operating-state controls

Add open/closed hours, temporary closure, handover blackout and “unable to receive” states. Buyers need to know when a hub is genuinely available, not merely verified.

6. Custody exception queue

Damaged parcel exists already, but lost/late arrival, wrong parcel, wrong recipient, repeated PIN mismatch, no-show pickup and unauthorized staff access need explicit paths into TrustOps.

7. Re-verification & suspension

Authorization can expire or the primary agent can change. A TrustOps lifecycle screen should pause only the affected custody permissions while preserving existing Trades and evidence.

8. TrustOps SLA + auditability

Every case needs owner, SLA clock, reason for reassignment, evidence request history and final decision. The existing Design System already establishes that decisions should be auditable and AI should suggest rather than decide.

UI/UX refinement I recommend across the whole Park Agent surface

Persistent hub identityKeep “Jibowu Park Hub” + Hub ID visible in the top shell.
One custody statusUse Active / Held / Suspended rather than many ambiguous labels.
Action-first dashboardPut Arriving, Awaiting Pickup and Exceptions ahead of earnings.
Evidence by defaultCamera capture should timestamp and attach hub identity automatically.
Reason before riskSuspensions, freezes and reassignments always show why and what remains usable.
Role switch clarityShow Buyer / Merchant / Park Agent as distinct modes with their own trust state.

Home — Additional States

Home actions and role-aware trade attention

The approved Home: one header carries the Buy / Sell switch, notifications and the account; below it the protected balance, three actions, what needs attention, active trades, recent activity and quick actions. The buyer navigation has five tabs (Home, Trades, Messages, Discover, Account); the merchant navigation has five (Shop, Orders, Listings, Messages, Account).

Trade Policies

The applicable terms are shown with the trade. Final outcomes depend on state, evidence and policy.

You can ask for more inspection time with a reason (up to 72h Electronics, 48h Fashion & Luxury). Eligibility and any refund follow the actual trade state.
Policy and state-machine alignment: cancellation is free before shipment; inspection windows are 48 hours for Electronics and 24 hours for Fashion & Luxury; reasoned extension requests are allowed (up to 72 / 48 hours); full-refund grounds include damaged, not-as-described or incomplete items. There is no universal change-of-mind return right. Backend enforcement, refund execution and payment reconciliation remain server responsibilities.
Agreement, funding, dispatch, delivery, inspection and completion4 mobile
Lifecycle Exceptions

Expiry, withdrawal, inspection and issue-intake states

Lifecycle outcomes and exception states that attach to the existing trade, delivery and resolution flows: expiry, withdrawal, inspection extension and issue intake.

↑ Master index
Design gap audit · reference notes
Gap 01 · Six-hour expiry outcome

The master shows a six-hour countdown and funded/unfunded paths, but no dedicated expired-trade screen that explains what happened and what each party can do next.

Gap 02 · Withdrawal consequence

The workspace has a withdrawal reason form, but the post-submit experience needs a clear recorded state and must distinguish an unfunded trade from a trade with money in motion.

Gap 03 · Inspection extension decision

BEI1 and BEI2 already cover request and seller review. The missing piece is a clear decision/result state that updates the inspection deadline without losing the original window.

Gap 04 · Item issue intake

The original screens include dispute filing, evidence and multi-item inspection, but the first issue-intake step should make reason, affected item(s) and evidence explicit before a case is submitted.

Policy ambiguity · Returns vs. disputes

The source screens support cancellation before shipment and disputes for item problems; they do not establish a universal change-of-mind return right. The designs therefore route problems to the applicable dispute/policy path without promising a return.

Service dependency · Delivery quote

TW-02 previews route pricing. A production courier quote must include provider result, validity and failure/retry handling; the current prototype estimate is not a live quote.

Agreement, funding, dispatch, delivery, inspection and completion9 mobile
Canonical Mobile Architecture — Trade Workspace · Tabbed

One Trade Workspace across the full transaction lifecycle

One canonical mobile surface for the full transaction lifecycle. The workspace creates no new trade state: it renders the authoritative trade, payment, fulfilment, inspection and case states in one role-aware context, with the same record shared by buyer and seller while the primary action changes by role, state and deadline. Flow: Agreement → Funding → Fulfilment → Delivery → Inspection → Resolution → Settlement → Closed. The five workspace tabs are now the Trade details rows, each opening its supporting screen.

↑ Master index
Pre-implementation structural audit · what was retained, corrected and deliberately not duplicated
Retained · TW-01The existing shared trade record, role switcher, six-hour expiry, withdrawal and funding guard remain the source design foundation.
Retained · TW-02 / policyDelivery method, courier quote dependency, Park charge logic and category inspection minimums remain aligned with the existing master.
Connected · lifecycle exceptionsExpiry, withdrawal, extension and issue intake remain separate outcomes; the workspace links to them rather than recreating their forms.
Corrected · one status is not enoughTrade state, payment state, fulfilment state, inspection state and case state are shown as related but distinct facts.
Corrected · financial language“Protected”, “processing” and “completed” are intentionally separated so the UI does not imply a ledger outcome before confirmation.
Corrected · action hierarchyEach state has one primary next action; secondary actions remain available only when valid for the current role and state.
Guard · state conflictsA production implementation must reject stale actions against the latest trade version and route the user to a re-review state.
Guard · deadlinesSix-hour trade expiry and inspection windows are displayed as deadlines, not decorative progress indicators; server time remains authoritative.
Guard · evidenceDispute evidence belongs to the case workflow. Chat is communication, not the authoritative evidence record.
Added · trade tabs + real flow buttonsThe five tabs are true filtered views of the same trade record. Focused actions still open the existing supporting screens for funding, dispatch, inspection, evidence, cancellation, refund and dispute workflows.

This pass extends the Park Agent lifecycle into a full TrustOps hub-management model. Park Hub onboarding is now explicitly treated as a TrustOps-owned case from application intake through approval, activation, permissions, custody incidents, suspension and re-verification. The existing PH1–PH7 screens remain the foundation; P13 adds the lifecycle states and TrustOps operating surfaces, while this extension adds Park Agents network management, New Hub registration, all-hub analytics, period filters, lifetime intake, held-parcel monitoring, and responsive left-pane navigation. The largest UX improvement is separating the hub entity from the person operating it, so staff can change without breaking custody history.

Other previously identified gaps remain represented in their existing sections — Seller Onboarding (SO1–SO5), Multi-Item Ship Order and Inspection (MI3–MI4), and real Two-Factor Setup (TF1–TF2).

PART 3Create & Propose a Trade — Canonical Desktop + Tablet

Komtru Living Master — Desktop Completion. Existing screens and the established component system remain the design authority. New desktop screens extend the same product language with desktop-native information density, split workspaces and operational context.
